blocks.intro: An insulated weld cannot be re-inspected: evidence is made at the bench.

items.q: Our specification says 3.1B certificates. Do you supply those?
items.a: 3.1B is the 1991 designation; EN 10204:2004 replaced it with 3.1. We supply 3.1 and note the equivalence. A 2.2 report is not accepted for product contact.
Our standard is [share of product-contact welds borescoped, %], stated in the plan. A weld that cannot be reached is accepted on its coupon, the reason logged.

items.q: What happens to a rejected weld?
items.a: It is cut out, not ground or re-fused. The replacement gets a new number and its own inspection, linked to the rejected weld. Rejection rate reported: [weld rejection rate reported, yes or no].

items.q: Can we audit the shop and see a real weld log?
items.a: Yes. Shop: [shop location, city and province]. Sample log: [redacted weld log shareable under NDA, yes or no].

items.q: Do we need electropolish, and who passivates?
items.a: Not by rule. SF1 is common for PW; we recommend SF4 for hot WFI, pure steam and tank interiors. Passivation by: [in-house or named subcontractor].
